hpx.native.transport.startup.title: Startup and process state
hpx.native.transport.startup.summary: Explicit workspace/TLS configuration; locked startup; process tokens.
hpx.native.transport.startup.description: run/main select workspace/create/port/certificate/private key; reject invalid paths/port/Unix key permissions and fail closed on TLS configuration. State starts without an unlocked Workspace; launch and session tokens are independent OS-random process-lifetime capabilities. A mutex serializes route handling. No trust installation, startup enrollment or release-time Node/Lean/database server.

hpx.native.transport.https.title: Bounded HTTPS and HTTP framing
hpx.native.transport.https.summary: Loopback rustls; bounded workers, request framing and socket deadlines.
hpx.native.transport.https.description: Numeric 127.0.0.1 listener; rustls/httparse; 16 worker slots, 16 KiB headers, 48 parsed headers, 14 MiB body and one ten-second socket deadline. Reject duplicate headers, transfer encoding, Expect, unsupported methods/framing and pipelined bytes already buffered; close each connection. Check deadline after acquiring the state mutex and before running a queued route; no cancellation of already executing storage/KDF work. TLS keys are distinct from workspace keys.

hpx.native.transport.security.title: Request, session and lock gates
hpx.native.transport.security.summary: Host/Origin and bootstrap/session checks; protected-data lock guard.
hpx.native.transport.security.description: route_inner checks exact numeric Host, cross-site requests and POST Origin/JSON type before dispatch. Static assets branch before session authentication. Bootstrap exchanges launch capability for a separate Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookie; duplicate session cookies fail closed. Runtime metadata and explicit lifecycle/status are available at their defined locked-state gates; other API calls require an unlocked workspace. Session identity is not document authority or decryption custody. Domain/resource authorization remains below these transport gates.

hpx.native.transport.assets.title: Embedded-asset routing
hpx.native.transport.assets.summary: Static GET lookup; no arbitrary disk serving or workspace unlock.
hpx.native.transport.assets.description: Non-API GET requests resolve only the generated embedded ASSETS map, including / to /index.html; return MIME-typed bytes or 404. Host/cross-site checks apply, but no session or unlocked workspace is needed to load the UI. Build.rs creates resources ahead of release; CodeMirror/KaTeX/editor logic runs in the browser. Response headers/CSP are written by the shared response path.

hpx.native.transport.api.title: API dispatch and wire adapters
hpx.native.transport.api.summary: API1 commands/queries; lossless conversion; progressive typed coverage.
hpx.native.transport.api.description: Route existing API1 calls after transport/session/lock gates. Forward frozen operation IDs and exact expected state; application/storage retain resource authority, receipts and transaction semantics. Committed Fork uses borrowed RawValue and lossless DTO/codec conversion; other commands retain legacy conversion. Scoped query handlers call existing workspace methods, not Workspace::execute. Canonical byte/ID distinctions and duplicate-field rejection are retained. Typed schema coverage is partial; documents/lock intentionally ignore request bodies. No general query engine, provider execution or complete target endpoint catalogue is implied.

hpx.native.transport.lifecycle.title: Workspace session lifecycle
hpx.native.transport.lifecycle.summary: Metadata, explicit passphrase/keychain actions and lock; Rust-only keys.
hpx.native.transport.lifecycle.description: State owns Option<Workspace>. Authenticated runtime/status can report supported/enrolled/locked state without revealing keys. Explicit passphrase creation/open is default; keychain unlock is an enrolled alternative, not automatic startup access. Shared one-second unlock throttle and mutex serialize attempts. Enroll/remove require unlocked owner; workspace keychain implementation verifies backup/upgrade/cleanup and current ownership. Lock drops the workspace; documents and lock retain ignored-body compatibility. This is transport lifecycle routing, not a new key provider, recovery protocol or grant of document authority.

hpx.native.transport.responses.title: Responses, errors and security headers
hpx.native.transport.responses.summary: Legacy JSON; opt-in problem details; no-store/CSP and connection close.
hpx.native.transport.responses.description: json/error/storage_error and route provide bounded stable codes with opt-in application/problem+json for routed LegacyError responses; malformed HTTP, expired queue and unavailable-state responses outside route remain legacy. write_response emits exact body length, close/no-store/nosniff/no-referrer and same-origin CSP. No response includes workspace keys or provider secrets. A transport timeout is not evidence that a publication failed; reconcile the original operation. Full target error/negotiation schema coverage remains partial.

hpx.native.transport.client_access.title: Future API / MCP access
hpx.native.transport.client_access.summary: Future client authentication/transport/scope design; not a live endpoint.
hpx.native.transport.client_access.description: Non-browser/MCP adapters must converge on the same application authority/expected-state/receipt semantics. Product client authentication, transport and scope remain unselected. Current local HTTPS can be exercised by isolated test clients, but is not delivery of the proposed MCP/remote API. Remote deployment, conditional WSS/event channels, multi-user login and client-held execution are not enabled or selected here.
